The reference asserted that finite scalar affine/activation graphs implement all positionwise maps, although the hard-model definition permits arbitrary multivariate fixed maps. Qualified it to the case where finite-network implementations are chosen. The actual Definition, earliest-key rule, fixed-length-independent maps, EOS readout and soft-model hypotheses are unchanged.

Step 6.1 used ReLU(z) as the residual correction, which leaves every negative coordinate unchanged. Replaced it by the allowed correction ReLU(-z), so z+ReLU(-z)=max(0,z). This zeros invalid negative states and preserves every nonnegative valid encoded state; finite code separation, pulses, and both lookup conclusions remain intact.

The exact-zero invariant is achievable, but the original explanation mentioned only attention values and positive pulse centers, omitting the nonzero detector shift and clipping that restore zero. Added that full invariant, stable finite-state softmax simulation, and a bound uniform in ramp widths and temperatures. These local proof gaps are repaired without changing either universality claim; no nonzero exterior output is asserted.
